title: Which write hits the watch?

milestone.title: Visual Studio and the Build Pipeline

description:
A data breakpoint watches `size` bytes starting at address `watch`. The program performs a series of memory writes; each `Write` has a starting address and a length in bytes.

Write `firstHit(writes, watch, size)`, which returns the index of the first write that touches **any** byte of the watched range, or `-1` if none does.

A write of `length` bytes at `address` touches the bytes `address` to `address + length - 1`. The watched range is `watch` to `watch + size - 1`. Two ranges touch if they overlap by at least one byte.

```
watch 0x1008, size 4  (bytes 0x1008..0x100B)
writes: { 0x1000, 8 }   bytes 0x1000..0x1007: just misses
        { 0x100C, 4 }   bytes 0x100C..0x100F: just misses
        { 0x1004, 8 }   bytes 0x1004..0x100B: hits      -> answer 2
```
hints: Two ranges, each given as a start and a length, overlap when the first starts before the second ends **and** the second starts before the first ends.
With "end" meaning one past the last byte: `writeStart < watchEnd && watchStart < writeEnd`. Using one-past-the-end values makes the edge cases come out right without any `- 1`.
